explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/1079 (proved by Bollobás–Thomason). For r ≥ 4 there is c > 0 such that every graph on n ≥ 2 vertices with at least ex(n;K_r) edges has a vertex v with d(v) ≥ cn whose neighbourhood spans at least ex(d(v);K_{r-1}) edges. The neighbourhood edge count is the number of edges with both ends adjacent to v. With the non-strict ≥, the Turán graph itself also satisfies the conclusion, since each neighbourhood is exactly T_{r-2}(d). So the page's caveat 'unless G is the Turán graph' does not create a counterexample here.
